title: Too Long, Didn’t Read? The Impact of Length Limits on Microblogging Engagement
authors: Shuting Ada Wang; Brad N. Greenwood
eligible_reason: Weibo extended its length limit for paid members in late January 2016 (Month 13; Wave 1) and for non-members in November 2016 (Month 23; Wave 2), but the two waves are estimated separately as single-date DiDs: Wave 1 columns (reghdfe ... Member1_After1 ... if Month<23, absorb(uid date)) have one treated cohort (members) and non-members as controls; Wave 2 columns (M_NM event-time terms, Month>=13) have one cohort (non-members) against already-treated members and add RM_Member1. No column pools both cohorts. All columns also include lagged/time-varying controls (l.CumVideoRatio, l.CumImageRatio, LnDaysSinceRegist, LnDaysSinceRegist_lnfans; lnPreCumulative* in post-level models). The Twitter/microWorkers and Chinese-university experiments are cross-sectional RCTs.
design_notes: Stata (reghdfe). User-day panel of 8,534 randomly sampled Weibo users, Jan 2015-Dec 2017 (User_Level_Data.dta, 23.6 GB) and post-level data (Post_Level_Data.dta). Timing checked in the data: After1 switches on in Month 13 (partial) and After2 in Month 23; Member1 is fixed (users who changed status dropped).

ineligible_specs_listed.location: Wave 1 user-day DiD and event study (Code.do lines 63-82, 110-114)
ineligible_specs_listed.reason: single adoption date within the Month<23 window; lagged and time-varying controls
single adoption date for non-members with already-treated members as controls; RM_Member1 extra regressor; controls
single adoption date; hour FE; time-varying controls

data_files_note: README: 'all data necessary to reproduce the results of the paper are included'; Weibo data scraped by the authors in 2020.
data_provenance_note: Full analysis sample of scraped Weibo users shipped (the random draw of 20,000 users is the authors' sampling frame, not a subsample of the analysis data).
screener_notes: Screened from README, Code.do, data timing check and OpenAlex abstract. The phased rollout has two cohorts, but each specification uses one wave only, so no published column is a staggered design; a pooled re-estimation would not reproduce any reported column.
